- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) and forecast spikes sharply, cap the forecast at 1.5x the recent 7-day average to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and forecast is low, add 0.10 to 0.20 to the forecast to avoid underestimating mean reversion.  
- After a forecast spike (e.g., > 2.5x recent average), reduce the next 3 days’ forecast by 15–30% to account for momentum correction.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, apply a 10–15% downward bias to forecasts when sentiment is trending downward.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the first 5 days show high volatility or extreme values, apply a 20–30% smoothing filter to avoid horizon-specific overreaction.  
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.8) and forecast is below true outcome, adjust upward by 0.10–0.20 per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- If sentiment is negative and forecast is above true outcome, reduce forecast by 0.15–0.30 per day to align with sentiment-driven correction.
